title: BAGMAN NeedsYouItem
description: Canonical `NeedsYouItem` (CD-6 Slice 1, PID §98.2/§98.5) — one entry in BAGMAN's universal, cross-domain operator queue: 'the small set of things a human must decide before BAGMAN can keep going'. A NeedsYouItem is deliberately NOT scoped to one BAGMAN domain (evidence intake, email triage, invoice review, rule approval, ...) — `item_type`/`domain`/`source_object_reference` together let any future producer raise a question here without this schema changing. `item_type` and `allowed_action_type` are both open (NOT closed enums, unlike `status`) so a later CD-6 slice (email classification, rule approval) can introduce a new value without a contract redesign — see `services.needs_you.needs_you`'s module docstring for the documented, non-exhaustive vocabulary this delivery already knows about (`COMPANY_REQUIRED`, `PURPOSE_REQUIRED`, `CLASSIFICATION_REVIEW`, `RULE_APPROVAL`, `GENERIC_QUESTION`) and for exactly which of these Slice 1's own real trigger (governed evidence intake reaching ACCEPTED/registered) uses.

item_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this Needs You item.

item_type.description: The kind of question this item asks. Deliberately open (NOT a closed enum) — see this schema's own top-level description and `services.needs_you.needs_you`'s module docstring for the documented, non-exhaustive vocabulary.

domain.description: The BAGMAN source module/workflow that raised this item, e.g. `EVIDENCE_INTAKE`, `EMAIL_TRIAGE`, `INVOICE_REVIEW`. Deliberately open for the same extensibility reason as `item_type` — a later slice introduces new producers without a contract change.

source_object_reference.description: The canonical BAGMAN object this item is about, e.g. an `evidence_id` (PID §98.5's own worked examples — 'Screwfix receipt', 'AWS invoice' — are both evidence-anchored). Required key, explicit `null` for an item that is not anchored to one single canonical object (e.g. a general operator question, PID §98.5's 'HMRC email' / 'Adobe rule' examples could be email- or rule-anchored instead once those domains exist) — never omitted, so 'not yet known' can never be confused with 'field left out by accident'. Also the natural key this delivery's idempotent-creation guarantee is keyed on together with `item_type` (see the repository's own docstring) — a replayed producer call for the same `(item_type, source_object_reference)` pair must resolve to the SAME item, never a duplicate.

question.description: Concise, human-readable question the operator must answer (PID §98.5's own worked examples, e.g. 'Which company is this for?').

allowed_action_type.description: What kind of answer/action this item expects, e.g. `COMPANY_WHAT_WHY` (Slice 1's own single real action type — see `services.needs_you.needs_you` module docstring). Deliberately open for the same extensibility reason as `item_type`/`domain`.

priority.description: Operator-facing priority/urgency bucket. A closed enum (unlike `item_type`/`domain`/`allowed_action_type` above) — PID §98.5 lists `priority` as a plain field with no extensibility requirement, and a small closed set is simpler for the GUI to sort/colour consistently.

status.description: Queue-item lifecycle state (this delivery's own documented, deliberately small state machine — see `services.needs_you.needs_you.ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS`): `OPEN` (awaiting an operator answer) -> `RESOLVED` (the operator answered it) or `DISMISSED` (the operator explicitly declined to answer it, e.g. not applicable). Both `RESOLVED` and `DISMISSED` are terminal — an item is never reopened; a producer that still has a live question creates a fresh item instead (mirrors `IntakeRecord.status`'s own closed, non-reopenable terminal-state doctrine, CD-4 PID §7).

created_at.description: UTC timestamp at which this item was raised.

resolved_at.description: UTC timestamp at which this item reached a terminal state (`RESOLVED`/`DISMISSED`). Required key, explicit `null` while `status` is still `OPEN`.

resolved_by_actor_type.description: PID §14 actor-type vocabulary value for whoever resolved/dismissed this item (operator provenance, PID §98.5's own 'operator provenance' field). `null` while `status` is still `OPEN`.

resolved_by_actor_id.description: The specific actor identity that resolved/dismissed this item (PID §14 — never a generic 'system' literal). `null` while `status` is still `OPEN`.

resolution.description: The operator's answer, shaped per `allowed_action_type` — e.g. for Slice 1's `COMPANY_WHAT_WHY`, `{"entity_id": ..., "what": ..., "why": ...}` (PID §98.3's Company/What/Why review interaction). Deliberately a free-form object rather than a typed-per-`allowed_action_type` union at this contract layer (Slice 1 has exactly one real action type; a future slice with a genuinely divergent shape can still be validated at the domain layer without a breaking contract change). `null` while `status` is still `OPEN`.

correlation_id.description: Identifier shared by this item's own creation/resolution AuditEvents and, where applicable, the upstream workflow that raised it (e.g. the same `correlation_id` as the `IntakeRecord`/`EvidenceItem` that triggered a `COMPANY_REQUIRED` item) — same correlation doctrine as `bagman.audit_event.v1.correlation_id` (PID §31).

metadata.description: Free-form, genuinely open context about this item (e.g. `evidence_id`/`original_filename`/`detected_mime_type` for an evidence-anchored item) — display/context only, never a substitute for `resolution` once answered.

schema_version.description: Contract version identifier for this NeedsYouItem. Must literally equal `"bagman.needs_you_item.v1"` for instances of this schema version.
